body:
I've done some more debugging, and it looks as though the issue isn't the checksum, it's that snappy is returning early from snappy.decode(in, out, maxLength)  [Line 266](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/master/codec/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/compression/Snappy.java#L266)

If I fake the length to send in (since the compressed, input buffer is 176 bytes long) to 176-12 (12 is the header), then the inputLength (preamble), read next off the input buffer is 405, which is clearly incorrect.  [Line 263](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/master/codec/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/compression/Snappy.java#L263)
Should be fixed in #1005 - I suck at bitmasks, but again have added another unit test to validate

I've just merged @lw346's fix. @CodeMason, could you confirm the fix? Here's the snapshot: https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/snapshots/io/netty/netty/4.0.0.Beta1-SNAPSHOT/netty-4.0.0.Beta1-20130201.042144-9.jar

The inputLength returned by readPreamble is the correct value - the uncompressed size of the incoming data.

However, the point remains about comparing compressed and uncompressedLengths, and is an oversight on my part.  Fixing this will be slightly more complicated then I thought, as we have no way of knowing how long the compressed data will be.  I guess I'll have to maintain more state inside the Snappy class and check the remaining value against each tag that I need to read.

@lw346
I just did some more testing. The uncompressed input size is 274, which is the size of the input (in the example above). Why would readPreamble on the compressed data return 402? Shouldn't it return 274? (or a value < 274?)
I fixed framing format and updated all test cases.  I also added a couple more tests that show `Snappy.encode/decode()` fails to decompress the data it compressed.
